checks: Persistent logical tombstone v13 rejects late full update v12 with an actual SQL version predicate.
Removing retained state lets the same v12 recreate the row; a version predicate alone has no forgotten floor.
For concrete two-part bytes, full SHA256 differs from SHA256 of concatenated part digests.
Two same-base updates after serialization have one winner and one failed condition; the second cannot silently overwrite.
Deleting an old physical generation leaves the distinct new physical generation intact; reusing a name does not.
limits: These are SQL predicate, checksum-byte and physical-identity counterexamples. They do not execute Elasticsearch, PostgreSQL, S3, object GC, leases or distributed fault handling. Service correctness also depends on the documented adapters, permissions and serialization contracts.
